deep.reconstruction:
Context: Göttingen, May–June 1818. Gauss is reducing meridian-circle observations of Arcturus (α Boo) and Polaris to obtain the latitude of the observatory. The previous page has Polaris readings of May 19; the next page applies the same scheme to γ And and to Arcturus for July–November.

(A) Mean declination of Arcturus carried to 1818.0 (top left). The catalogue value for 1815 is δ = 20°9'2.60". The annual variation is −19.01"/yr, so three years give −57.03" and δ(1818.0) = 20°8'5.57". The '21' overwritten by '20' is a correction of the degree figure. The value −19.01"/yr is consistent with precession 20.05"·cosα plus Arcturus's proper motion in declination of about −2"/yr (my identification). The logarithms set up the daily rate and the day count: log 19.01 = 1.27898, log 365.25 ≈ 2.56256, and their difference 8.71642 (i.e. −10) gives 0.05205"/day. log 132 = 2.12057, since May 12 is day 132 of the year, and log 172 ≈ 2.2355 for June 21. The entry '40161' is unexplained.

(B) Arguments for the periodic terms (top right table). The rows are for May 12, May 22, Jun 1, Jun 11 and Jun 21; all entries are degrees.minutes.
- Column 1 is the Sun's longitude ☉: 51°31', 61°7', 70°40', 80°13', 89°43'.
- Column 2 is the Moon's node ☊: 38°9', 37°37', 37°5', 36°33', 36°2' (decreasing about 32' per 10 days).
- Column 3 is 2☉.
- The header constants 298°25', 320°9' and 326° are phase angles for this star.
- The log row 1.0949 | 0.9002 | 9.664 gives the amplitudes 12.44", 7.947" and 0.461".
- The rows beneath are log sin(☉+298°25'), log sin(☊+320°9') and log sin(2☉+326°); 'n' marks a negative sine.

The resulting terms for Arcturus are therefore:
- aberration: Δδ_ab = 12.44" sin(☉+298°25');
- lunar nutation: Δδ_N = 7.947" sin(☊+320°9');
- solar nutation: Δδ_S = 0.461" sin(2☉+326°).

My check of these amplitudes and phases, with α ≈ 211.9°, δ ≈ 20.13°, ε ≈ 23.47°:
- Aberration: Δδ = κ(cosα sinδ sin☉ − (sinε cosδ − cosε sinα sinδ) cos☉). Its amplitude is 0.6143κ, which equals 12.44" for κ = 20.25"; the phase is about 298.4°.
- Lunar nutation: Δδ = Δψ sinε cosα + Δε sinα. The written form corresponds to Δψ ≈ −18.0" sin☊ and Δε ≈ 9.66" cos☊, i.e. the older nutation constant of about 9.6".
- Solar nutation: the written form corresponds to Δψ ≈ −1.13" sin2☉ and Δε ≈ 0.49" cos2☉.

(C) Apparent declination table. Each row has four corrections:
- precession and proper motion since 1818.0: −6.89, −7.41, −7.93, −8.45, −8.97 (0.052"/day);
- aberration: −2.17, −0.10, +1.96, +3.98, +5.87;
- lunar nutation: −0.24, −0.31, −0.38, −0.46, −0.53;
- solar nutation: +0.43, +0.46, +0.44, +0.37, +0.26.

The apparent declination is 20°8'5.57" + Σ, written as seconds over 20°7' (the header reads 19°7' corrected to 20°7'). This gives 56.70, 58.21, 59.66 and 61.01 for the first four dates. Jul 1/11/21 are left blank and continued on the next page.

(D) Latitude from Arcturus. At upper culmination south of the zenith, φ = δ_app + z, where z is the reduced circle reading.
- May 12: 31°24'19.88" + 20°7'56.70" = 51°32'16.58".
- May 17: 31°24'14.63" + 56.85" = 51°32'11.48".
- May 19: 31°24'15.87" + 57.76" = 51°32'13.63".
- The mean of these three is 51°32'13.90" + δ.

After May 19 the readings jump by about 50", evidently an instrumental change such as reversal or resetting of the circle, which is why the two groups are kept separate.
- May 20: 31°23'29.23" + 57.91" = 51°31'27.14" (marked ::, doubtful).
- May 21: 23'17.90" + 58.06" = 51°31'15.96" (marked ::).
- May 22: 23'23.98" + 58.21" = 51°31'22.19".
- May 24: 23'25.97" + 58.50" = 51°31'24.47".
- May 25: 23'27.20" + 58.65" = 51°31'25.85".
- The mean of the three unmarked values is 51°31'24.17" + δ.

The mean of the two groups is 51°31'49.03" + δ. Here δ is the unknown correction to Arcturus's tabular declination (and anything else common to the star). Comparing with the Polaris latitude 51°31'51.02" gives δ = +1.99".

(E) Latitude from Polaris, lower and upper culmination, in two instrumental groups.
- Lower culmination, group 1: 51°32' + (16.67, 17.84, 19.55, 17.36, 19.50); mean 51°32'18.18" − δ.
- Lower culmination, group 2 (from the 21st): 51°31' + (24.96, 27.16, 27.44, 25.69, 22.80, 20.14); mean 24.70" − δ.
- Upper culmination, group 1: 32' + (16.07, 19.50, 12.75, 18.81); mean 16.78" + δ.
- Upper culmination, group 2: 31' + (25.52, 20.35, 24.76 on the 25th, 20.30 on the 29th); mean 22.73" + δ.
- Averaging the two groups gives lower 51°31'51.44" − δ and upper 51°31'49.76" + δ.
- Since a declination error enters the two culminations with opposite signs, the mean 51°31'50.60" is free of Polaris's declination error. The implied (unwritten) Polaris correction is δ = (51.44 − 49.76)/2 = +0.84".

The 50.60" at the bottom differs from the 51.02" used for the Arcturus comparison above, apparently an earlier or alternative Polaris value.
errors: Jun 21 apparent declination: with the correct lunar-nutation term −0.53 (the sequence −0.24, −0.31, −0.38, −0.46, −0.53 and the n-sign of the log both require a minus), the sum gives 5.57−8.97+5.87−0.53+0.26 = 2.20, i.e. 62.20, but 62.30 is written (0.10" slip). With +0.53 it would be 63.26. The value is not used further on this page.

May 17 Arcturus: the declination 56.85 is the value for May 13 (56.70 + 0.15). Linear interpolation for May 17 gives about 57.46. Either the date is 13, not 17, or the declination is about 0.6" too small, which would make the May 17 latitude about 0.6" too small.

The Arcturus correction δ = +1.99" is derived from the Polaris latitude 51°31'51.02", whereas the Polaris reduction at the bottom of the same page gives 51°31'50.60". With the latter, δ would be +1.57". This is an inconsistency between two Polaris values, not an arithmetic error.
Minor: log 365.25 = 2.56259 (2.56256 written) and log 172 = 2.23553 (2.23559 written); differences of a few units in the fifth decimal, negligible.
The Jun 21 lunar-nutation log, read as 8.8292n, should be 8.8233n (sin 3°49'); either a misread or a slip. The product still gives about −0.53.

results.what: Reduction of Arcturus's mean declination 1815→1818 with annual variation −19.01"/yr, and day-fraction precession/proper motion (0.05205"/day)
results.modern_name: Reduction from mean place to epoch (precession plus proper motion)

results.what: Aberration in declination for Arcturus written as 12.44" sin(☉+298°25'), and nutation terms 7.947" sin(☊+320°9') and 0.461" sin(2☉+326°), evaluated by logarithms
results.modern_name: Apparent-place reduction with star constants (precursor of Besselian day numbers / star-specific constants)
results.usually_credited_to: Bradley (aberration 1729, nutation 1748); tabular form of star constants systematized by Bessel (Tabulae Regiomontanae 1830)

results.what: Latitude from zenith distances of Arcturus (φ = δ + z) in two instrument settings, and from upper and lower culminations of Polaris (declination error cancels), giving φ ≈ 51°31'50.6" and a correction of +1.99" to Arcturus's declination
results.modern_name: Determination of latitude from circumpolar star at both culminations; calibration of a star's declination

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine observatory reduction work (apparent places, latitude from Polaris at both culminations) of the kind known from Gauss's 1818 Göttingen observing activity. The only modest interest is the documentary detail: the specific star constants, including Arcturus's proper motion within the 19.01"/yr, and an early value of Göttingen's latitude of about 51°31'50".

checkable.asserts: aberration amplitude for Arcturus ≈ 12.44" with κ = 20.25"
mean of the three unmarked Arcturus values = 24.17 (the five-value mean would be 23.12)
Polaris upper group 1 mean = 16.78 (requires first value 16.07)

transcription_corrections: Top left: '[-21-]20 9' 2" 60' is 20°9'2.60" (degree figure 21 corrected to 20). This is Arcturus's declination, and likewise 20°8'5.57".
Header over the apparent-declination column reads 19°7' corrected to 20°7'; the values 56.70 etc. are seconds over 20°7'.
Top-right table entries are degrees.minutes: e.g. 38.9 = 38°9', 37.5 = 37°5', 61.7 = 61°7'.
Jun 21 lunar nutation entry should be −0.53, not +0.53.
Jun 21 log in the second column is probably 8.8232n (8.8292n as transcribed is inconsistent with sin 3°49').
First upper-culmination (Ober) Polaris value is 51°32'16"07, not 16"67; the mean 16.78 requires 16.07.
May 20 and 21 Arcturus readings carry '::' doubt marks and are excluded from the mean 24.17.
The second Arcturus date may be May 13 rather than 17, judging from the declination 56.85 used.
